result.process_description:
Title: Service for Your Fridge

Your fridge produces strange noises.
You describe the symptoms, and send them together with the type of fridge to the central fridge service center.
They select a local service facility (which all have their own way of interacting with customers).
The service facility makes an appointment.
They arrive at a random time, and sometimes have to leave without repairing your fridge, because they need additional parts.
After your fridge is repaired, you have to confirm that it is OK again.
You can rate the service facility.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

args.text: When a description says work may be unsuccessful because a required resource is unavailable, model the success and unavailable-resource outcomes as conditional branches, with the unavailable-resource path obtaining the resource and returning to the relevant work or scheduling step.

result.rule: When the description states that an activity is required while another activity may be performed only if a stated condition holds, and that the flow continues after the applicable work is complete: Model the activities as branches from an inclusive split, with the condition on the optional branch, and use an inclusive join to synchronize the branches that were activated before the dependent next step.

When the description says that several work items must each pass an evaluation before a later step can proceed, and that unsuccessful items require revision and another evaluation: Model an outcome decision for each work item, route unsuccessful items through the required revision and back to evaluation, and synchronize the successful paths before the dependent step.

When the description says an optional activity may occur after a later activity, and that each occurrence causes that later activity to happen again: Model the optional activity on a conditional return path to the later activity, while preserving the path that continues without the optional activity.

When the description states that an activity's result or a condition determines which of multiple alternative paths follows: Connect the activity to an exclusive gateway and model each alternative as a separate outgoing branch.
